title: Attestation slab pricing + ephemeral evidence token flow for rapid enterprise on-ramp
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise deals are frequently delayed by long security questionnaire cycles and the ad-hoc evidence assembly required for SIG/CAIQ. Large customers ask for signed, time-bounded attestations and up-to-date evidence bundles; Sales and SE teams spend manual hours producing bespoke packages.

Proposal: Implement a two-part offering: (1) a purchasable 'attestation slab' (prepaid bundles of signed attestations and evidence credits sold in tiers) and (2) an 'ephemeral evidence token' that packages a signed, verifiable snapshot of a CAIQ subset + pointer to an immutable audit snapshot. Tokens are short-lived (default 30 days) and can be minted in the Console or via an API for SEs to attach to proposals.

Key goals: Reduce average sales cycle time for security review by 30%, lower SE/manual evidence work by 40%, and increase conversion of mid-market to enterprise trials by 12%. Provide a productized, auditable attestation flow that scales without manual legal involvement for common asks.

Scope: Console purchase and token UX, backend token signer service (KMS/HSM integration), templates for common CAIQ sections, pricing slabs, billing hook for slab consumption, audit-log events, API endpoint for minting/verifying tokens, and minimal legal templates for templated signed attestations. Does NOT include bespoke legal negotiation or long-form third-party audit generation (out of scope).
acceptance_criteria: Console: buyer can purchase an attestation slab from pricing tiers (Lite/Standard/Premium) and see remaining credits in billing dashboard
API: authenticated SE can mint an ephemeral evidence token bounded to a CAIQ subset; token contains signed hash and pointer to immutable evidence snapshot
Security: token signing uses customer/KMS-integrated HSM path where required; all token issuance and usage are recorded in the audit log
Tracking: instrumented metrics for slab purchases, token mints, tokens attached to proposals, and time-to-contract reductions
Legal: templated attestation text approved by Legal for use with slabs and ephemeral tokens
Experiment: A/B test framework in place comparing slab buyers vs per-section pay-as-you-go on conversion and NRR
success_metrics: 30% reduction in median security review duration for deals using tokens within 90 days
40% drop in SE-manual evidence assembly hours (measured by time-logging pilot team)
12% lift in trial->paid conversion for mid-market customers enrolled in the slab pilot
Gross margin on slabs >= 65% after implementation costs
experiment_design: Run an initial pilot with 12 strategic accounts (mix of mid-market and enterprise): half offered attestation slabs, half offered per-section pay-as-you-go credits. Track time to finish security questionnaire, number of manual evidence requests, and deal conversion. Concurrently expose slabs to self-serve in Console with an optional SE assistance checkbox. Evaluate after 8 weeks and decide on roll-out. A/B grouping randomized by account segment and weighted toward accounts with prior questionnaire friction.
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: backend token signer prototype + KMS proof-of-concept (ENG). Week 3: Console purchase flow + billing integration (PM/ENG/Design). Week 4: Legal templates finalized and security review completed. Week 5-8: Pilot with 12 accounts (Sales/SE). Week 9: Evaluate metrics and iterate; if success gates met, expand to GA with marketing collateral and pricing page updates.
tradeoffs: Slab pricing could cannibalize higher-margin bespoke evidence work but reduces manual cost and speeds deals. Short token TTL reduces stale claims but may frustrate buyers who need long-term evidence; mitigate by offering evidence snapshot export for audits. Implementing HSM-backed signing increases engineering complexity and time-to-market but is necessary for enterprise trust.
risks: Legal/regulatory: signed claims may be treated as representations in contracts—Legal wants guardrails. Technical: KMS/HSM integration and key rotation complicate ops. Commercial: pricing slabs may shift negotiation leverage with large buyers. Adoption: sales must be trained to use tokens correctly to realize time savings.
open_questions: What is the default token TTL and will customers be allowed to extend?
Do we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for on-prem/private deployments in v1 or v2?
What subset of CAIQ sections are most valuable to include in a first template?
How do we present slabs vs pay-as-you-go in the Console without causing choice paralysis?
data_and_tracking: Events: slab_purchase, token_mint, token_verify, evidence_snapshot_download, security_questionnaire_closed. Dashboards: per-account token usage, time-to-contract for token vs control, SE time-savings. Tracking PR: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/analytics/pulls/213. Example Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/attestations/attestation-usage
notes_and_comments: 2025-09-13 — Scoping sync: agreed to implement both Console and API flows in pilot. (Aisha)
2025-09-20 — Design review: low-friction purchase drawer to avoid bouncing SEs out of workflow; design to provide quick copy for emails. (Noor)
2025-09-26 — Legal feedback: prefer explicit non-representative language and log-forwarding to avoid contract exposure; requested prototype templated language. (Markus)
2025-09-30 — Security review kickoff: initial concerns on key management; recommended HSM-backed signer in GA. (Priya)
2025-10-02 — Engineering: prototyped token signer using KMS shim, initial PR created for token format and API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1429 (Mateo)
2025-10-02 — Sales ops: identified 12 pilot accounts and proposed SE playbook for token usage. (Hannah)
next_steps: Finalize legal templated language (owner: Markus) by 2025-10-06; complete HSM/KMS proof-of-concept and merge prototype PR (owner: Mateo) by 2025-10-10; instrument pilot analytics and onboard pilot accounts (owner: Hannah) by 2025-10-14.
notes_for_sales: SEs will receive a 1-page playbook on when to use a token vs request bespoke evidence. Tokens are not a replacement for SOC2 or audited reports; they are meant to accelerate initial security review cycles.
estimated_costs: Initial engineering + security effort estimated at ~10 engineer-weeks and one-time HSM integration cost (infra) approximated at $18k. Ongoing marginal cost per token is expected to be low (crypto signing + storage).
final_decision_if_pilot_successful: GA with 3 slab tiers, public pricing page, and API docs. Offer CMK support in a paid add-on for Dedicated/Private customers in the following quarter.
